header.name: Schedule Events
header.description:
The Schedule Events flow will take a list of "Scheduling Groups" and schedule them in FIFO order. When dependencies are provided, the lowest level child dependency will be provided first and any references to it's ID in dependencies will move the earliestStart date out until it has completed.

Group Event Type Configuration:

1. available - This time is available for scheduling and will decrement the duration.
2. unallocated - There is not availability nor is it unavailble during this time. We cannot schedule anything in this range that will be worked on.
3. allocated - This is firmed up work that will be on the workcenter between the start/end. This will be handled as a blocker
4. reserved - If we are inside the firm window reserved is treated as allocated. If we are looking outside of the firm window reserved is treated as available.
5. informational - As the name states, these are informational events and are treated as available.

version.description:
- Updates to validate the availability calendars provided have a duration associated with them.
- Standardized the error output of the scheduler to include the \`schedulingError\` property.
- Updated the flow to stop once one distribution in the chain can't be scheduled. Any additional distributions from that point forward are useless anyway as nothing will be comitted.
- Updated the flow to enforce a 30 days (In milliseconds) max for the Distribution groups.

e00a93d2-26fe-48e6-8a0c-a3f395bb5e30.name: Reset Context
e00a93d2-26fe-48e6-8a0c-a3f395bb5e30.note:
Logic for looping with multiple dependencies the logic is fairly simple.

If we find that distribution we just scheduled has a dependency, we need to check it's current earliestStart. If it's earliestStart is later we leave it alone. If it's earliestStart is earlier then the end of the event we just scheduled we will shift it out. 

That way we're only comparing a single earliest start to an ends at and don't have to worry about finding both and taking the latest. This also means if someone provides an earliest start that's further out than the completion of anything else we can correctly apply that earliest Start so the distribution doesn't actually start then.
